Jordan - quick technical breakdown to clarify Dedicated vs Private VPC from a data isolation standpoint:

- Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed):
  * Compute: dedicated GPU pools reserved for FinSecure within Redwood's infrastructure.
  * Control plane: Redwood-managed. Control plane signals (routing, routing decisions) pass through Redwood, but you can configure policies to avoid logging payloads in the control plane.
  * Data flows: model inputs/outputs are processed on dedicated compute nodes; by default, request/response metadata (timings, routing) are visible to Redwood. Payloads can be configured to avoid storage/logging.
  * KMS: we support customer-managed keys for disk encryption; HSM integrations available as part of an enterprise package.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  * Compute: runs in your VPC or on-prem environment.
  * Control plane: option for customer-managed control plane (control API endpoints in your VPC) or a hybrid where control plane signals are brokered but payloads never leave your network.
  * Data flows: no egress of payloads from your VPC when configured in private mode. Logs (request/response) can be retained in your logging stack; we can ship agents (or integrate with your S3/CloudWatch) to push logs on-prem.
  * KMS: can be configured to use your KMS with full key custody; HSM options supported.

Short answer to your question: Dedicated capacity can be configured to minimize exposure, but if FinSecure policy requires absolute zero egress of payloads outside your network and customer-managed control plane, Private VPC/on-prem is the recommended path.

I'll bring a short topology diagram to the follow-up call.

Great questions - see answers below and attached artifacts.

- Private VPC (customer-managed control plane): typically a one-time onboarding/engineering fee (covers control plane deployment, network setup, and audit integrations) plus a recurring platform license (monthly). Exact numbers depend on throughput and HA requirements; I'll get a ballpark by EOD after a quick sizing with engineering.
- Dedicated capacity: usually a monthly committed capacity contract with optional burst credits. Term lengths commonly 12-24 months for the committed tier; we can provide short-term trials on a smaller committed pool.
- Compliance artifacts: attaching our SOC2 snapshot. We can also provide recent pen-test summary under NDA.
- Yes, Redwood can sign a standard DPA - please attach and we'll route to legal.
